sourcedFrom: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) (2021 ("© 2021 CZ-USA, All Rights Reserved.", PDF p.2))
cleanIntro: The Scorpion 3+ field strips into four groups: the receiver with its barrel, the trigger unit, the bolt with its recoil spring, and the magazine. One captive disassembly pin holds the trigger unit in, and the bolt is held back on the charging handle while it comes out. It is a 9x19mm semi-automatic, and CZ's owner procedure stops at the field strip. Everything below is from CZ-USA's own CZ Scorpion 3+ instruction manual.

steps.title: Magazine out — index finger on the ambidextrous release
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard. Grasp the pistol grip with one hand and the magazine with the other, press the ambidextrous magazine release with your index finger and pull the magazine straight down and out.
steps.prose: This is where the 3+ differs from the older EVO: the release is a button worked with the index finger, not a catch worked with the thumb. Hold the magazine as you press, so it comes out under control rather than dropping. The magazine coming out does not make the gun safe — the chamber is the next step, and it is the one that matters.
steps.quote: Press the ambidextrous magazine release with your index finger (Fig.2) and simultaneously remove the magazine by pulling it downward.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Operating Instructions — Removing the Magazine, p.10
steps.warn: Removing the magazine does not unload the pistol, and does not prevent the pistol from firing!

steps.title: Chamber emptied and checked with the bolt locked open
steps.action: With the safety selector set to "fire", pull the charging handle fully to the rear; a round in the chamber will be ejected. Push the charging handle upward while it is at the rear to lock the bolt open, then look into the chamber and confirm it is empty.
steps.prose: The selector has to be on fire for this — CZ's unloading sequence sets it there before the charging handle is pulled. Locking the handle up is what lets you look without holding the bolt back by hand, and it lets a second person check the chamber too. Check it by sight and by feel: CZ's own warning is to check the chamber both visually and physically.
steps.quote: By pushing the charging handle upward when in the rear position, you can lock the bolt in the open position so another person can inspect the chamber to verify it is empty
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Operating Instructions — Unloading the Firearm, p.12
steps.warn: Unload your pistol properly, including checking the chamber both visually and physically.

steps.title: Eye protection on, selector on fire
steps.action: Put on shooting glasses or goggles. Then, with the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty, set the safety selector to "fire" — it is a numbered step of CZ's disassembly, not a leftover from unloading.
steps.prose: Springs come out of this gun during the strip — the recoil spring leaves with the bolt — so eye protection is CZ's first instruction in the maintenance section. The selector on fire is the third step of their disassembly list, before the bolt is locked and before the pin is touched; skipping it is the easy mistake, because the gun looks no different either way.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly, step 3, p.13
steps.warn: Wear shooting glasses or goggles to protect your eyes from flying parts such as springs, which may be released during disassembly.

steps.title: Bolt to the rear and locked there on the charging handle
steps.action: Pull the bolt to the rear with the charging handle and lock it open by rotating the handle upwards. The bolt is now locked in the rear position.
steps.prose: This is the same lock you used for the chamber check, now doing the work of holding the bolt out of the way while the trigger unit comes out. If the handle will not stay up, the bolt is not far enough back — bring it fully rearward and rotate the handle again rather than forcing it. A bolt that slips off the lock runs forward under spring pressure, so keep your fingers out of its path.
steps.quote: 5. Move the bolt to the rear position with the charging handle and lock it open by rotating the handle upwards (Fig.8) The bolt is now safely locked in the rear position.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly, step 5, p.13

steps.title: Press the disassembly pin through and pull it out to its stop
steps.action: Hold the pistol grip tightly in one hand. With the thumb of the other hand push on the front of the trigger unit while you press the outer part of the disassembly pin, then withdraw the pin from the other side and pull it out to its most protruding position.
steps.prose: The pin is captive: it comes out to a stop and stays in the gun, so do not keep pulling once it stops. The thumb pressure on the front of the trigger unit is what takes the load off the pin so it will move. If the pin will not move, check that pressure before reaching for anything else — this is a hand operation in CZ's procedure.
steps.quote: Push on the front of the trigger unit with the thumb of the other hand and press the outer part of the disassembly pin (Fig.9). Now withdraw the captive disassembly pin from the other side and pull to its most protruding position.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly, step 6, p.13

steps.title: Trigger unit down and out at the magazine well
steps.action: Grasp the trigger unit case at the magazine well and pull it downward, out of the receiver.
steps.prose: The magazine well is the handle here — it is the solid part of the trigger unit and gives you a straight downward pull. Once the trigger unit is out, the underside of the receiver is open and the bolt and recoil spring can come out the same way. Set the trigger unit down as one piece; CZ goes no further into it.
steps.quote: Grasp the trigger unit case at the magazine well and pull it downward removing it from the Scorpion. Now it is possible to remove the bolt and the recoil spring.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly, step 6, p.13

steps.title: Bolt and recoil spring out through the bottom
steps.action: Move the bolt slightly backward with your thumb and pull it downward to remove it, together with the recoil spring.
steps.prose: The small rearward push takes the bolt off the charging-handle lock; then it drops out through the open bottom of the receiver. Keep a hand under it — the recoil spring comes out with it and is still a spring. Do not let the bolt run forward inside the receiver instead of coming down.
steps.quote: 7. Move the bolt slightly backward with the thumb and pull it downward to remove it.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly, step 7, p.13

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Receiver with barrel, trigger unit, bolt with recoil spring, and magazine — four groups. That is the whole disassembly CZ publishes for the Scorpion 3+; the barrel, handguard, charging handle and the trigger unit's internals all stay assembled.
steps.prose: These groups reach everything CZ's cleaning section asks for: the barrel and chamber from the chamber end, the bolt and its guide rails, the inside of the receiver, and the lubricating points in their diagram. CZ's instruction straight after step 7 is that nothing more is needed for routine maintenance, and the caution under it says not to go further — work beyond this is CZ-USA's Technical Support & Gunsmithing department's.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is required for routine maintenance. CAUTION: Do not disassemble the firearm any further.
steps.cite: Instruction Manual — CZ SCORPION 3+ — V.9 (printed on the last page, PDF p.24) — Maintenance Instructions — Disassembly, closing note, p.13

deepAbsentReason: CZ-USA's CZ Scorpion 3+ instruction manual (V.9) publishes no procedure past its seven-step disassembly. Step 7 is followed immediately by "No further disassembly is required for routine maintenance. CAUTION: Do not disassemble the firearm any further." and a direction to contact CZ-USA's Technical Support & Gunsmithing department for anything that needs more (p.13). Everything after that point in the book is cleaning, preserving and lubrication of the field-stripped groups, plus removing the rear head attachment and moving the pistol grip and charging handle — adjustments, not a second level of disassembly. The book gives the owner no bolt, striker, extractor or trigger-unit strip, so there is nothing further to walk.

cleaning.name: BARREL & CHAMBER
tasks: Unfired or only a few rounds: clean patch on the included cleaning rod through barrel and chamber, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean
Dirty barrel: apply firearm cleaning solution with a brush, let it act about 10 minutes, then scrub the bore thoroughly
Rod and brush go in from the CHAMBER end, and the brush is pushed all the way through before you reverse it — reversing inside the barrel sticks the brush
Nylon or copper-bristled brush in the chamber, then wipe it clean and dry
Dry barrel and chamber with clean patches and check that all powder residue and fouling is gone

cleaning.name: BOLT, RECEIVER & TRIGGER UNIT
tasks: Dry cloth, old toothbrush, copper-bristle brush or wooden scraper on the bolt, the receiver and the trigger unit — preserving oil can be used for a thorough clean
Clean the bolt and its guide rails — dirt there can leave the bolt stuck in the rear position while firing
Never use the bore-cleaning solvent on these parts — it stays in crevices and causes corrosion over time
Check that no cloth particles or brush bristles are left lodged in any part

cleaning.name: PLASTIC MAGAZINES
tasks: Heavily soiled, or for regular maintenance: disassemble the magazine and clean the plastic parts with detergent
Let the parts dry slightly, then leave them to air dry fully before reassembling the magazine

cleaning.name: PRESERVING
tasks: With barrel, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in firearm oil or apply a spray oil
Oil the lubricating points in CZ's lubrication diagram (Fig.10), which marks heavy-oil and light-oil points separately, then remove all excess oil
At very low temperatures, remove the oil from all accessible parts or use a lubricant intended for those conditions
Thick preserving grease is for long-term storage in severe climates only, and comes off every part before use
If the rear head attachment was removed, the receiver surfaces may be smeared with a preserving agent intended for plastics (graphite grease is CZ's example) before it goes back on

reassembly: CZ's whole reassembly instruction is to reverse the disassembly steps; this is that order.
Bolt with its recoil spring back up into the receiver from below, and locked to the rear on the charging handle.
Trigger unit back up into the receiver at the magazine well.
Push the captive disassembly pin back through to its seated position.
Rotate the charging handle down off its lock and let the bolt go forward.

If the rear head attachment was removed: press the rear head retaining button, slide the attachment base down onto the rails at the rear of the receiver to its lowest position, and listen for the click of the button locking in.
Before shooting, pull a dry patch through the bore to confirm it is clean and clear.
fncheck: Magazine out and chamber confirmed empty. With the safety selector on "0" the firearm must not fire; on "I" a trigger pull should drop the hammer once, and the trigger should need to be released before it will fire again. Pushing the charging handle up at the rear should lock the bolt open, and rotating it down should release it. Check that the disassembly pin is fully seated, that the trigger unit sits fully home in the receiver, and that a magazine locks in securely and drops free when the ambidextrous release is pressed.
